rivals.name: Composio
rivals.thesis: Composio is a hosted service that connects agents to apps through its SDKs and MCP, with sign-in handled on its side. Glyph Connect is a Mac and iPhone app that shows the tools your agents can already reach, from the app registry in your own vault.
short: Composio is a developer platform with an API key; Glyph Connect is an app with no account.
Composio runs your tool calls on its servers; Glyph Connect reads what is on your machine.
Both can limit single tools and mark read-only ones.
rivals.pick: Pick Composio if you are building an agent product and want hundreds of app connections and sign-in handled for you.

price: Free: $2 one-time credit, 10,000 tool calls a month. Standard $18 a seat a month, coming soon
platforms: Web dashboard, Python and TypeScript SDKs, MCP
account: Yes, an API key from the dashboard
perms: Yes, allow or block tools by name per session
writes: Yes, read-only and destructive tags, assigned best effort

rivals.name: Zapier MCP
rivals.alt_title: A free, local Zapier MCP alternative
rivals.thesis: Zapier MCP lets an agent run actions in the apps you have connected to Zapier, with each call billed against your task quota. Glyph Connect does not run actions; it shows every tool your agents can reach and lets you switch them off.
short: Zapier MCP uses two tasks per tool call; Glyph Connect is free.
Zapier MCP runs on Zapier's side; Glyph Connect reads your own vault.
Both separate read actions from write actions.
rivals.pick: Pick Zapier MCP if you want an agent to act in thousands of apps you already connect through Zapier.

price: In every Zapier plan; each tool call uses 2 tasks. Free 100 tasks a month, Pro from $19.99 a month billed yearly
platforms: Web setup; Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and other MCP clients
runs: Hosted by Zapier, set up at mcp.zapier.com
perms: Yes, you pick the actions in managed mode
writes: Yes, separate read and write action tools

rivals.note: Price figures: the task quota comes from zapier.com/pricing (source 3); the two-tasks-per-call rule from source 1.

rivals.name: Docker MCP Toolkit
rivals.alt_title: A free Docker MCP Toolkit alternative, no Docker needed
rivals.thesis: Docker MCP Toolkit runs MCP servers on your machine, each in its own container, inside Docker Desktop. Glyph Connect runs no servers; it shows the tools your agents already reach, which need you, and what each may read or write.
short: Docker's Toolkit needs Docker Desktop; Glyph Connect is a plain Mac and iPhone app.
Both run on your own machine.
Docker switches single tools off from the command line; Glyph Connect does it with one tap.
rivals.pick: Pick Docker MCP Toolkit if you want to install and run MCP servers in isolated containers from a catalog of 300+ verified servers.

price: Docker Personal $0. Paid plan needed in firms over 250 staff or $10M revenue
platforms: Docker Desktop on Mac, Windows, Linux
runs: On your machine, each server in a container
perms: Yes, enable or disable single tools from the CLI

rivals.note: The paid-plan threshold for larger companies is on https://docs.docker.com/desktop/setup/install/mac-install/. The Toolkit is a beta feature turned on in Docker Desktop settings.
